chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Goodly cheerfulness removes grudges.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of showing good cheerfulness in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on good cheerfulness, this hadith links the Prophet’s teaching to Imam Musa al-Kazim, emphasizing that a pleasant countenance (husn al-bishr) serves as a social lubricant that dissolves resentment. In Shia ethical tradition, this virtue is not merely superficial politeness but a profound spiritual discipline that fosters unity (tawarrud) and reflects inner tranquility. It complements the Quranic command to forgive with gentleness, positioning interpersonal warmth as a key mechanism for maintaining communal harmony.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The goodly cheerfulness does away with the grudges’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’a from abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Delightful appearance removes ill will.’”
